core_lesson_learned: The fertile frontier is the CAPABILITY-GAP (a domain whose existing ML lacks the specific capability a fresh technique uniquely provides), not the DOMAIN-GAP. Session 2 sharpened this with a hard sub-lesson: EVEN IN THE HIGHEST-FERTILITY REGION (neural operators x physics-bearing crafts), the craft's INDUSTRIAL ANALOG almost always already hosts the technique-family - blast/ladle-furnace thermal-state ML (vs bloomery), physics-informed FNO for tunnel-fire temperature fields (vs anagama kiln), shrinking-core/rotary-kiln calcination models (vs lime clamp), PINN full-field quench surrogates + real-time virtual thermal sensors (vs interrupted artisan quench), ViscNet/GlassNet glass-viscosity ML + digital glass-forming control (vs glassblowing), fixed-model ML foaming prediction (vs digester). So the artisan-scale + irregular-geometry + specific-tacit-judgment slice is genuinely unmade, but it is NARROW (capability-gap), NOT OPEN. HYPOTHESIS for OPEN: target crafts whose INDUSTRIAL ANALOG DOES NOT EXIST, so the technique-family has no prior foothold to make it NARROW.

life_domain_fertility.domain: Physics-bearing crafts WITH an industrial analog (glassblowing, kiln firing, forge/heat-treatment, smelting/bloomery, lime/brick burning, slag/tap)
life_domain_fertility.why: Dominate the 'none' AI-penetration bucket and have no consumer-app market - ideal for neural-operator/PDE-surrogate techniques. BUT each has an INDUSTRIAL analog that already hosts the technique-family, capping results at capability-gap NARROW. Most defensible slices: traditional CLAMP lime-burning (thinnest adjacency), traditional BLOOMERY smelting.

life_domain_fertility.domain: Physics-bearing crafts WITHOUT an industrial analog (HYPOTHESIZED OPEN region - UNTESTED)
life_domain_fertility.why: If a craft's physics has NO modern industrial counterpart, the technique-family has no prior foothold and the gap could be truly OPEN. Candidates to source: highly idiosyncratic/obsolete or culturally-specific physical processes with documented physics but no industrial equivalent.
